text: I learned healing practices from my mother.
She believed most sickness came from imbalance in the body's humors, not the spirits.
I have treated injured animals since I was young.
Most injuries come from predictable causes: terrain, weather, workload.
But not all.
Some animals recover unusually fast when left near the river below the old platform.
I cannot explain why.
Other animals fail to recover in the same conditions.
Patterns are inconsistent.
Gopala trusts animal behavior more than human explanations.
I agree with him more than I admit.
During the aftermath of the ash from Kalinga, I saw injuries I couldn't classify.
Some wounds healed strangely.
Others worsened without infection.
Temple explanations didn't satisfy me.
But I did not argue.
Certain herbs grow only near specific stone formations.
Those formations appear in both the forest and the terrace fields.
I've mapped some of these locations privately.
I have not shared those maps.
Tarala often brings me plants she finds while wandering.
Some aren't common in the known grazing zones.
Bhumaka once asked why animals avoid certain irrigation areas.
I did not have a satisfying answer.
Marisha believes some losses are unavoidable.
I believe some losses are preventable but not yet understood.
Nara says healing is also spiritual balance.
I cannot measure spiritual balance.
But I can measure recovery rates.
They do not always match expectation.
